requirements.text: Check for any that are still queued and update them to failed status if they were never sent
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_003' AND incident_id = 'INC_001' AND status = 'failed'
assumptions: 'our major SAP outage incident' is INC_001 'MAJOR:SAP Database Unreachable' (description 'Major outage declared'; critical, in_progress); the other SAP incidents (INC_044, INC_069, INC_082) are neither major nor outages

NOTIF_003 is the only queued notification on INC_001 on the seed, so the task changes exactly one row and it is anchored by id; 'never sent' read as status = queued (the opened and delivered ones were sent)

disagreement: cells: A also tests incident_id = INC_001, B tests status alone; kept A's (the tighter predicate) because the row must be the SAP incident's notification and the seed ties NOTIF_003 to INC_001

requirements.text: send an update notification to the incident caller ... about the current status and resolution progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE incident_id = 'INC_001' AND email = 'thomas.green@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%status%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%progress%'
assumptions: the caller of INC_001 is USER_001 Thomas Green, thomas.green@servicenow.com (seed); the user is inactive on the seed, but the request names the caller and the policy's active-user rule covers assignment and updates, not notification recipients
three notifications are created and the request fixes no order, so the row is selected by incident and recipient, not by id
'update notification' read as type = update; the benchmark's type LIKE '%updat%' is tightened to that, the only enumeration value that matches
'current status and resolution progress' tested as the keywords status and progress, as the benchmark check does; the seed's NOTIF_002 to the caller has neither, so the count is measurable
subject and status are not tested: neither the request nor the benchmark check fixes them

requirements.text: remind the assigned person ... about the current status and resolution progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE incident_id = 'INC_001' AND email = 'gregory.richards36@servicenow.com' AND type = 'reminder' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%status%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%progress%'
assumptions: INC_001 is assigned to USER_059 Gregory Richards, gregory.richards36@servicenow.com (seed)
'remind' read as type = reminder, as the benchmark check does
selected by incident and recipient, not by id (three notifications are created)
subject and status are not tested

requirements.text: remind ... managers of the group about the current status and resolution progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE incident_id = 'INC_001' AND email = 'christina.oliver@carsonllc.com' AND type = 'reminder' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%status%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%progress%'
assumptions: the group is INC_001's assignment_group GROUP_008 L2 Infra Team; its manager_id is USER_002 Christina Oliver, christina.oliver@carsonllc.com (seed), read as the manager of the group, as the benchmark check does
USER_002 is a reporter in ORG_002 on the seed, yet is the recorded manager of GROUP_008; the seed's value is used
'managers' (plural) read as the group's manager_id only; member Cheryl Osborne (USER_049) has the manager role but is not the group's manager, and a reminder to her is neither required nor forbidden
selected by incident and recipient, not by id (three notifications are created)
subject and status are not tested

requirements.text: Check for any that are still queued and update them to failed status (boundary: queued notifications on other incidents are not touched)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_024' AND status = 'queued'
assumptions: selector boundary: NOTIF_024 (INC_096, a Monitor incident) is the only other queued notification on the seed and belongs to a different incident, so it must stay queued

requirements.text: update them to failed status if they were never sent (boundary: the sent notifications on the incident are not failed)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id IN ('NOTIF_001', 'NOTIF_002', 'NOTIF_005') AND status <> 'failed'
assumptions: selector boundary: INC_001's other notifications were opened or delivered on the seed, so 'never sent' does not cover them and they must not be marked failed; anchored by id so the agent's new notifications for INC_001 do not alter the count

disagreement: form of this stay: A names the three rows with status <> 'failed' as the cell (expected 3), B selects the rows with status = 'failed' and no cells (expected 0); kept A's, which names the rows the boundary protects, the two being equivalent

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the four benchmark checks (all kept), the incident (INC_001), the queued notification marked failed (NOTIF_003), the three created notifications (update to the caller Thomas Green, reminders to the assignee Gregory Richards and to the group's manager Christina Oliver, each selected by incident and recipient because the request fixes no order) and the two boundary stays (the queued notification of another incident, the sent ones of INC_001). Both passes read 'managers of the group' as the group's recorded manager (user_group.manager_id = USER_002), which the benchmark checks; the other reading is group members with the manager role, which would add USER_049 Cheryl Osborne (cheryl.osborne@servicenow.com); no requirement is written for her, since the schema fixes one manager per group, the benchmark tests only that one, and the plural does not plainly ask for her. The caller Thomas Green is inactive on the seed; the request names him regardless.
disagreement: cells of the NOTIF_003 change: A tests incident_id = INC_001 and status = failed, B status alone; kept A's, the tighter predicate, because the row must be the SAP incident's notification (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: form of the three created-notification requirements: B repeats the selector's columns (incident_id, email, type) in cells, A keeps only the message predicates there; kept A's because cells hold what is tested beyond the selector, the convention of the other check files, the SQL being identical.
disagreement: form of the LIKE predicates in cells: A prefixes LOWER(message), B writes the bare predicate; kept B's, the convention of every other check file, the SQL being identical.
disagreement: form of the sent-notifications stay: A names the three rows with status <> 'failed' as the cell (expected 3), B selects by status = 'failed' with no cells (expected 0); kept A's, which names the rows the boundary protects (logged on the requirement).
